items.title: U.S. Efforts to Tighten Blockade of Iran Rely on Reluctant Neighbors
items.summary: Washington wants to intensify its economic pressure campaign on Iran by closing its land borders. Neighboring states, fearing economic fallout, are pushing back.

items.title: Seeking to Broaden Ukraine Talks, U.S. Urges Russia to Include Europe
items.summary: As a round of negotiations ended in Abu Dhabi, President Trump’s envoys said they would go to Moscow as the Kremlin demands discussions on European security structures.

items.title: Workers in Spain Stage a General Strike for the First Time in 14 Years
items.summary: Workers in a wide range of industries walked off the job to protest rising rents and stagnant wages, which have become central issues in the campaign.

items.title: Alexander Darchiev, Russia’s Ambassador to the U.S., Dies at 66
items.summary: The death of Alexander Darchiev was announced by Russia’s foreign ministry. He was appointed to his post in Washington in 2025, as relations between the Kremlin and the White House warmed.

items.title: Nvidia Scandal Unveils a Fierce Spy War Raging Behind Trump and Xi’s Diplomacy
items.summary: That the United States suspected Nvidia’s leader was a Chinese spy target underscores the deep distrust between the two powers, even as their leaders try to stabilize ties.

items.title: Kenya Starts Countdown to End of Ebola Outbreak
items.summary: The milestone is further evidence that African countries have mostly succeeded in preventing community transmission and isolating the small number of cases that have come in from Congo.

items.title: On Dakar’s Packed Beaches, Africa Welcomes Its First Youth Olympics
items.summary: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games are taking place in Senegal, where the beaches and streets are teeming with sports fans and fitness fanatics.

items.title: Lots of Competition to Catholicism in Peru as Pope Returns for Visit
items.summary: Pope Leo spent nearly two decades in Peru, rising to bishop and becoming a citizen. But many Peruvians have turned to evangelical churches, seeking a more expressive and direct connection to God.

items.title: Lebanon Faces Economic ‘Catastrophe’ After War and Years of Mismanagement
items.summary: Hezbollah’s conflict with Israel and the U.S.-Israel war with Iran have made systemic problems worse, causing the cost of living to soar and driving many Lebanese to despair.

items.title: This Defense Makes Drones (and GPS) Think They’re in Peru
items.summary: GPS-linked devices have been insisting that Ukrainians are in Lima, the Peruvian capital. The culprit is a jamming system built to thwart Russian airstrikes.

items.title: Nvidia’s Stock Price Plummets as Board Is Said to Consider Jensen Huang, CEO’s, Future

items.title: United Airlines Blocks A.I. Agents From Booking Flights
items.summary: The carrier said that to protect customers’ information and comply with regulations, it was barring the digital assistants from logging into accounts and managing reservations.

items.title: Jensen Huang Said to Have Had Relationship With Nvidia Executive Who Reports to Him
items.summary: Mr. Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, is already facing scrutiny over an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence determined was a Chinese spy.

items.title: Court Rules That Sexual Harassment Case Against SpaceX Can Proceed
items.summary: The company had argued that the case, involving eight former workers, must be resolved before an arbitrator.

items.title: Trump Officials Clashed Over Megaspeed, Firm at Heart of Nvidia Affair

items.title: Silicon Valley Tech Allies Support Jensen Huang
items.summary: Elon Musk and other Silicon Valley figures cast the Nvidia chief’s relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy as a personal lapse, not a security failure.

items.title: How GLP-1 Drugs and a Revamp Revived Ro’s Business
